correctness.rationale: By independence along the unique tree path and linearity of expectation, each origin score is its distance-count polynomial, including the common constant 1. Independently enumerated all unlabelled trees through order 14 by adjoining one leaf to every vertex of each previous representative and merging equal canonical rooted codes at the tree centers. Removing a leaf establishes completeness inductively; equal canonical codes imply isomorphism and the center set is invariant. The shape counts for orders 1–14 are 1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23,47,106,235,551,1301,3159. Checked exact score comparisons after factoring out p(1-p). A fixed strict Bernstein sign removes a globally dominated score; at most one Descartes variation makes each surviving dominance set an interval. Grouped equal score profiles so ties cannot masquerade as unique winners. For the six order-13 and seventeen order-14 exceptions, independently isolated the roots of one square-free rational polynomial per shape covering all nonidentical surviving comparisons (16 and 44 interior roots respectively), and evaluated the full set of maximum scores at exact rational points in every intervening open cell. All discrepancies near isolated roots are covered by the adjacent constant-sign cells; isolated points cannot themselves furnish an open reentry interval. No smaller tree reenters. For the specified 15-vertex witness only 1 and 2 survive, with the stated profiles. The difference quartic is positive at both endpoints, negative at 1/2 and strictly convex on (0,1), with the two indicated roots. Origin 1 beats every other noncandidate strictly on the full open domain, confirming the 1,2,1 sequence and both two-way ties.
residual_risks: This is an exact finite census with an independent tree generator and rational polynomial calculations, not proof-assistant verification. It does not bound reentry for larger or cyclic graphs.

originality.rationale: Existing work covers decay centrality, one top-ranked switch, prescribed pairwise crossings or full-ranking instability. The strongest inspected catalogue analogues use nonuniform source weights on paths or the same homogeneous expected-reach objective on graphs with cycles. None establishes the sharp order-15 boundary for the exact homogeneous tree model and strict global reentry. A closely related subscription article remains an explicitly unresolved source, not evidence for or against coverage.
residual_risks: The 2026 article could contain stronger results in uninspected text. No priority or exhaustive absence claim is inferred from catalogue dates or bounded retrieval.

value.rationale: The natural optimization problem distinguishes complete rankings or nonoptimal crossings from an actual change in the best seed. Its smallest counterexample to absence of strict global reentry is a useful sharp boundary: the exact finite lower bound rules out every smaller unweighted tree, and the explicit witness identifies the two switches rather than sampling or relying on pairwise reversals.
residual_risks: No implications are established for multiple origins, heterogeneous transmission, arbitrary graphs, or empirical policies.
